subject: Hosted vs Dedicated decision follow-up (latency / throughput)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-28T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

1) Summary of FinPay requirements from today
- Workload: real-time payment risk scoring (API calls per payment)
- Peak: ~2,500 qps during peak windows; steady-state 400–600 qps
- Latency target: p95 < 100ms for inference response end-to-end
- Data residency: must remain in us-west region; no shared GPU persistence of PII

2) Deployment options we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest to go-live, auto-scaling, Redwood-managed infra; may have slightly higher p95 in spike scenarios unless we use burst/reserved capacity
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for FinPay, predictable throughput and lower p95; stronger isolation and custom autoscaling policies
- Private VPC/on-prem: discussed briefly — likely not necessary for initial pilot given your requirements but open if compliance requires it later

3) Immediate ask from FinPay (please confirm)
- Confirm target p95 and expected sustained qps for a 1-hour peak period
- Are you able to commit to a 30-day pilot with a light monthly minimum for Dedicated if we show it meets p95?

4) Next steps I propose
- You send any finalized qps/latency numbers (or confirm what we captured) — Alex
- We run a short benchmark on Hosted API and Dedicated (same model variant) and share load test results — Redwood
- Follow-up call to review results and recommendation: target Tue/Thu next week

Attachments: finpay-qps-latency-requirements.xlsx (xlsx) — please confirm numbers in sheet.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Thanks Neha — this looks right. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Confirmed: peak 2,500 qps sustained for ~30–45 minutes during settlement windows; sustained daytime 450 qps.
- Target: p95 < 100ms end-to-end for the model inference (we accept some network/transit overhead but want inference p95 ~<80ms if possible).
- Data residency: must stay in us-west and logs need to be retained for 90 days.

We are open to a 30-day pilot, but for procurement we need an estimated committed monthly spend if we go Dedicated (ballpark). Also need to see load-test numbers for Hosted vs Dedicated to present to security/procurement.

Can you run tests against our staging endpoints? I can share API keys with a short-lived scope.

Attachment: load_test_results_20270528.csv (sample traffic from our internal sim)

Appreciate it —
Alex Jensen
Head of Platform Engineering, FinPay

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Neha / Dylan —

Saw Alex's note. Recommendation for the benchmark plan and proposal: 

1) Benchmark plan (we'll run both Hosted API and a Dedicated pool configured to FinPay QPS):
- Model: redwood-rt-medium (same variant for parity)
- Scenarios: 450 qps steady-state (1 hour), 2,500 qps stress test (45 minutes), and spike test (5 minute ramp to 3,000 qps)
- Metrics: model p95, CPU/GPU utilization, queueing latency, token cost per request
- Data: run from us-west region; use FinPay staging API key (short-lived)

2) Dedicated config proposal (initial):
- 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (pooled), autoscale headroom for bursts + configured burst queueing policy
- Expected inference p95: ~60–85ms depending on request payload and batching; consistent throughput at 2,500 qps in our sim
- Monthly commit estimate: $85k–$95k (ballpark) — needs final pricing from finance but gives procurement a number to evaluate

3) Deliverables: load test report (CSV + summary), recommended deployment mode, SOW draft if they want to proceed to pilot

I'll prep a short Dedicated config PDF and an SOW template. Dylan, can you schedule the benchmark runs for Monday (us-west) and capture detailed logs?

-Marissa
Director of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

- We'll share raw CSVs and a 1-page exec summary within 24 hours of the runs
- Pricing: preliminary Dedicated commit estimate $85k/month (for 8 A100-equivalent pool) — I'll follow up with formal quote and SOW. Hosted pricing for this QPS would be higher variability; we'll include a cost-per-token comparison in the report.

If that schedule works, can you send the staging API key with an expiry of 48 hours? We'll only use it for the scheduled runs.
